briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B as National Psychedelics Wave Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's legal cannabis market just blew past a massive lifetime sales milestone, and operators are rallying behind a gubernatorial candidate who's vowed to kill the 24% wholesale tax squeezing margins. Nationally, the FDA is fast-tracking psychedelic medicine, Eli Lilly just bought into the space, and a federal court win keeps marijuana's Schedule III momentum intact.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17B in lifetime legal weed sales — Michigan has now surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales, generating an estimated $2.66 billion in state excise and sales taxes.

Industry throws weight behind tax-cut candidate for governor — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association has officially endorsed Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, citing his commitment to repealing the controversial 24% wholesale tax.

Jars Cannabis wins fight to pull police camera — Jars Cannabis confirmed it reached an agreement with the city to remove a Flock surveillance camera after recent uproar concerning surveillance at its retail location on 12 Mile Road.

U.P. chain grows by splitting the tax bill with suppliers — Rize, which operates three Upper Michigan locations, has managed to sustain growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers, splitting the tax burden rather than absorbing it alone.

Wholesale tax revenue misses targets, fueling repeal push — Revenue for Michigan's controversial 24% wholesale tax on marijuana continues to fall short of projections in its first year, and a Republican state representative has filed legislation to reverse the tax after it generated less than half of the $420 million lawmakers projected.

national.text: FDA pushes psychedelic medicine toward the mainstream — the agency is moving toward possibly greenlighting psilocybin and methylone after President Trump ordered an acceleration of federal research, fast-tracked FDA reviews and expanded patient access to psychedelic treatments.

Eli Lilly closes its blockbuster psychedelics buyout — the AtaiBeckley acquisition by Eli Lilly, approved by stockholders September 8 and expected to close September 11, brings BPL-003, VLS-01 and EMP-01 under Lilly's development umbrella.
DEA advances bid to move psilocybin off Schedule I — the DEA has advanced a petition to move psilocybin from Schedule I to Schedule II, now under Department of Justice review.

Court leaves medical marijuana's Schedule III move intact — a lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's rescheduling was rebuffed this week when the D.C. Circuit court left the reclassification order in effect, finding opponents had not demonstrated grounds to block it.

Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora escalates into proxy fight — Curaleaf's initial $272 million hostile takeover bid claims a 45% premium, but Aurora's board rejected the offer unanimously and is urging shareholders to follow suit, with Curaleaf's CEO firing back that Aurora has never presented a counteroffer.
